# Introduction

PM2.5 is particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometers. It is one of the
most dangerous air pollutants. The particles are small enough to go deep into
lung tissue and into the bloodstream, where they cause cardiovascular and
respiratory disease. Delhi is consistently one of the most polluted megacities
in the world. In the winter months (October to January), PM2.5 concentrations
routinely exceed the WHO safe limits by a factor of 10 or more.

This vignette uses two independent data sources in the `vayuayan` package to
analyze the air quality of Delhi in 2022. The two sources together answer one
policy question:

> Do the 46 CPCB ground monitoring stations give sufficient coverage of the
> full spatial extent of pollution in Delhi? Or do some regions have too few
> monitors, so that the network systematically misses their PM2.5?

The analysis has four steps:

1. The seasonal trend shows if the satellite data and the ground data agree on
   the pollution cycle of Delhi.
2. The spatial heatmap shows where pollution in Delhi is highest.
3. The station network map shows the locations of the 46 sensors relative to
   that pollution.
4. The monitoring gap analysis finds which of the 290 wards are farthest from
   their nearest sensor. It also finds if that distance predicts the
   disagreement between ground and satellite data.

---

# Data and methods

## Satellite data

The monthly PM2.5 estimates come from the V5GL04 product of the Washington
University in St. Louis Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group (WUSTL ACAG).
V5GL04 is a global gridded dataset at ~0.01° (~1 km) resolution. It comes from
satellite retrievals of aerosol optical depth, chemical transport models, and
ground-level calibration (van Donkelaar et al., 2021). The files are in NetCDF
format.

V5GL04 covers 1998 to 2022. For 2023 and later years, you must use V6GL02.
The departmental server does not have the V6GL02 download yet. This vignette
uses 2022 data in all sections.

## Ground data

`cpcb_download_city_data()` and `cpcb_download_station_data()` get the daily
city-level and per-station PM2.5 readings from the Central Pollution Control
Board (CPCB) data repository. Delhi has 46 operational Continuous Ambient Air
Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS). DPCC, CPCB, IMD, and IITM manage these
stations. `cpcb_add_coords()` gets the station coordinates directly from the
CPCB live feed. The function uses Nominatim as a fallback only for stations
that are temporarily absent from the live feed.

## Spatial units

The ward boundaries come from the BharatViz Delhi ward dataset
(`geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/delhi.geojson`). This dataset has 290
wards and covers all of Delhi, with the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC)
area. All spatial analyses in this vignette use this one boundary file.

## Comparison caveat

The two data sources measure PM2.5 differently:

- A satellite value is the spatial mean over a full area (~1 km pixels).
- A ground value is a point measurement at one physical location. Ground
  stations are often near pollution sources.

Thus, the ground readings are consistently higher than the satellite
estimates. This difference comes from point-source measurement against
area-averaged measurement. It is not an error. For a fair comparison in time,
the analysis aggregates the ground data to monthly means.

# Setup

```{r packages}
library(vayuayan)
library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(tidyterra)
library(exactextractr)
library(ncdf4)
library(khroma)
library(here)
```

```{r folder-setup}
vignettes_dir <- here::here("vignettes")
data_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "data/delhi")
fig_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "figures/delhi")
station_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "station_data")

for (d in c(data_dir, fig_dir, station_dir)) {
  dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}
```

## Satellite reads

The satellite values come from WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 monthly files. The package
downloads these files (Asia subset) one time from the AWS Open Data registry
into `nc_dir`. `pm25_monthly()` gives the mean over the bounding box of a
region. `pm25_load_netcdf_bbox()` gives the cropped raster.

```{r nc-dir}
nc_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "data/pm25")
```

---

# Results

## Seasonal trend

### Ground data: city-level monthly PM2.5

```{r ground-data}
delhi_ground <- cpcb_city_daily("Delhi", 2022, cache_dir = data_dir) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(value), .groups = "drop")

print(delhi_ground)
```

### Satellite data: monthly spatial mean over Delhi

```{r satellite-data}
delhi_shape <- sf::st_read(
  "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/delhi.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% sf::st_make_valid()

delhi_sat_df <- pm25_monthly(delhi_shape, 2022, version = "V5GL04", region = "AS", cache_dir = nc_dir) %>%
  rename(sat_pm25 = pm25)

delhi_final <- inner_join(delhi_ground, delhi_sat_df, by = "month")
print(delhi_final)
```

### Seasonal line chart

```{r line-chart, fig.cap="Delhi 2022: monthly PM2.5 from satellite and ground sources. Both sources agree on the seasonal pattern, with a peak in winter and a minimum in the monsoon. Ground readings are consistently higher because of the difference between point and area measurement."}
ggplot(delhi_final, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite"),
    linewidth = 0.85, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite"), size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = "dotted", color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15, linetype = "dotted", color = "orange", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text",
    x = 1, y = 18, label = "WHO 24hr limit (15 µg/m³)",
    size = 3, color = "tan4", hjust = 0
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = 1, y = 8, label = "WHO annual limit (5 µg/m³)",
    size = 3, color = "darkgreen", hjust = 0
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "CPCB Ground"     = "#d77027ff",
    "WUSTL Satellite" = "#4575b4"
  )) +
  labs(
    title   = "Delhi 2022: PM2.5 seasonal cycle, satellite vs ground",
    y       = expression(paste("PM2.5 Concentration (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),
    x       = NULL,
    color   = NULL,
    caption = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text               = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linetype = "dashed", color = "grey85"),
    legend.position    = "top"
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig1_seasonal_trend.png"), width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

The line chart shows that both sources agree on the seasonal pattern. PM2.5
peaks sharply from October to January and decreases during the monsoon. Delhi
exceeds the WHO limits in every month. Ground readings are ~2× higher than
satellite values. This agrees with the difference between point and area
measurement.

For 2023 to 2025, ground data is available. The satellite data for these years
(V6GL02) is not yet on the departmental server.

## Spatial heatmap

```{r heatmap-data}
nov_file <- pm25_download_netcdf(2022, 11, version = "V5GL04", region = "AS", cache_dir = nc_dir)
r_nov <- pm25_load_netcdf_bbox(nov_file, delhi_shape)
delhi_raster_mask <- pm25_load_netcdf_bbox(nov_file, delhi_shape, mask = TRUE)
delhi_city_boundary <- sf::st_union(delhi_shape)
```

```{r heatmap, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Spatial PM2.5 distribution across Delhi, November 2022. Blue outline = Delhi boundary. Peripheral areas have higher PM2.5 than central Delhi."}
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = delhi_raster_mask) +
  geom_sf(
    data      = delhi_city_boundary,
    fill      = NA,
    color     = "royalblue4",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  scale_fill_whitebox_c(
    palette = "muted",
    name    = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")"))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Spatial distribution of PM2.5, Delhi",
    subtitle = "Satellite estimate: November 2022 | Blue outline = Delhi boundary",
    caption  = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 | Resolution: ~1 km"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig2_heatmap_nov2022.png"), width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

The heatmap shows that pollution is not uniform. Peripheral areas have higher
PM2.5 than central Delhi. The next section shows that these areas also have
fewer monitoring stations.

---

## Station network choropleth

### Load and geocode station locations

```{r station-coords}
station_file <- file.path(data_dir, "delhi_stations_with_coords.csv")
if (file.exists(station_file)) {
  delhi_station_list <- read.csv(station_file)
} else {
  delhi_station_list <- cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi")
  delhi_station_list <- cpcb_add_coords(delhi_station_list)
  write.csv(delhi_station_list, station_file, row.names = FALSE)
}

delhi_full_sf <- delhi_station_list %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat)) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

cat(nrow(delhi_full_sf), "stations loaded\n")
```

### Choropleth: ward-level PM2.5 and station locations

```{r choropleth-data}
delhi_wards <- delhi_shape
delhi_wards$sat_pm25 <- exactextractr::exact_extract(
  r_nov, delhi_wards, "mean",
  progress = FALSE
)
```

```{r choropleth, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Ward-level satellite PM2.5 with CPCB station locations. Stations cluster in central Delhi. The current network gives poor coverage to several peripheral wards with higher PM2.5."}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = sat_pm25),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_full_sf, color = "black",
    fill = "steelblue4", size = 2.5, shape = 21, alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    na.value  = "grey80",
    name      = expression(paste("Sat PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi PM2.5 monitoring network",
    subtitle = "Ward shading = satellite average PM2.5 | Blue dots = CPCB stations",
    caption  = "November 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig3_choropleth_stations.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

The choropleth shows that the stations cluster in central and south Delhi.
Several peripheral wards with relatively high PM2.5 have few or no sensors
near them.

---

## Monitoring gap analysis

This section answers the primary question. Which wards have too few monitors?
Does the distance to a sensor predict the disagreement between ground and
satellite data?

### Concept

For each of the 290 BharatViz wards, the analysis does these steps:

1. Find the geographic centroid of the ward.
2. Find the nearest CPCB station and its winter ground PM2.5 reading.
3. Extract the satellite PM2.5 at that centroid.
4. Calculate delta = satellite − nearest ground station.
5. Draw a line from the centroid to the nearest station.

### Per-station winter ground data

```{r winter-ground}
station_ground <- cpcb_station_daily(
  delhi_station_list$value, 2022,
  cache_dir = station_dir
) %>%
  filter(month %in% c(1, 10, 11, 12)) %>%
  group_by(station_id) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(value), .groups = "drop")

station_ground_sf <- station_ground %>%
  left_join(delhi_station_list %>% select(value, lat, lon),
    by = c("station_id" = "value")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

cat(nrow(station_ground_sf), "stations with valid winter PM2.5\n")
```

### Compute delta at each ward centroid

```{r compute-delta}
ward_centroids <- sf::st_centroid(delhi_wards)

sat_centroid_vals <- terra::extract(r_nov, terra::vect(ward_centroids))
delhi_wards[["sat_pm25_centroid"]] <- sat_centroid_vals[["lyr.1"]]

dist_matrix_winter <- sf::st_distance(ward_centroids, station_ground_sf)
nearest_idx <- apply(dist_matrix_winter, 1, which.min)

delhi_wards$nearest_ground_pm25 <- station_ground_sf$ground_pm25[nearest_idx]
delhi_wards$nearest_winter_km <- apply(dist_matrix_winter, 1, min) / 1000
delhi_wards$delta <- delhi_wards$sat_pm25_centroid -
  delhi_wards$nearest_ground_pm25

delhi_wards <- delhi_wards %>%
  mutate(
    priority = case_when(
      nearest_winter_km > 2 &
        sat_pm25_centroid > median(sat_pm25_centroid, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "High priority",
      nearest_winter_km > 2 ~ "Medium priority",
      TRUE ~ "Well monitored"
    )
  )

cat("Delta summary (satellite - nearest ground station):\n")
print(summary(delhi_wards$delta))
cat("\nPriority breakdown:\n")
print(table(delhi_wards$priority))
```

### The monitoring gap map

```{r gap-map, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Monitoring gap map. The color of each ward shows the ground-satellite disagreement. Dashed lines connect each ward centroid to its nearest CPCB station. Yellow dots = CPCB stations."}
centroid_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(ward_centroids)
station_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(station_ground_sf)[nearest_idx, ]

connection_lines <- data.frame(
  x_from = centroid_coords[, 1],
  y_from = centroid_coords[, 2],
  x_to   = station_coords[, 1],
  y_to   = station_coords[, 2],
  delta  = delhi_wards$delta
) %>% filter(!is.na(delta))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = delta),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = connection_lines,
    aes(x = x_from, y = y_from, xend = x_to, yend = y_to),
    color = "grey8", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.6, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = station_ground_sf,
    color = "black", fill = "yellow",
    size = 2.5, shape = 21, alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = khroma::colour("roma")(100),
    values = scales::rescale(c(
      min(delhi_wards$delta, na.rm = TRUE),
      median(delhi_wards$delta, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(delhi_wards$delta, na.rm = TRUE)
    )),
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = expression(paste(Delta ~ PM[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi: satellite vs nearest ground station PM2.5 by ward",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines connect each ward centroid to its nearest CPCB station\nColor shows relative difference | Yellow = CPCB stations",
    caption  = "Delta = satellite PM2.5 at ward centroid − nearest CPCB station reading\nNovember 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig4_monitoring_gap_map.png"), width = 9, height = 7.5, dpi = 300)
```

### Priority map

```{r priority-map, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Priority wards for new CPCB stations. Red = high pollution and poor sensor coverage (>2 km from nearest station). Orange = poor coverage only. Green = well monitored."}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = priority),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_full_sf,
    color = "black", fill = "yellow",
    size = 3, shape = 21
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "High priority"   = "#d6604d",
      "Medium priority" = "#fdae61",
      "Well monitored"  = "#4dac26"
    ),
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Monitoring priority"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi: priority wards for new CPCB monitoring stations",
    subtitle = "Red = above-median PM2.5 and >2 km from nearest sensor\nOrange = >2 km from sensor | Green = well covered | Yellow = existing stations",
    caption  = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS | November 2022"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    text          = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig5_priority_map.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

### Sensor distance vs disagreement

```{r scatter, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Relation between sensor distance and ground-satellite disagreement across 290 Delhi wards. The LOESS fit with 95% CI can show a non-linear trend."}
cor_val <- cor(
  delhi_wards$nearest_winter_km,
  abs(delhi_wards$delta),
  use = "complete.obs"
)
cat("Correlation (distance vs |delta|): r =", round(cor_val, 3), "\n")

ggplot(
  data = sf::st_drop_geometry(delhi_wards),
  aes(x = nearest_winter_km, y = abs(delta))
) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.3, color = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(color = nearest_winter_km), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess", se = TRUE,
    color = "firebrick", fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = max(delhi_wards$nearest_winter_km, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.55,
    y = max(abs(delhi_wards$delta), na.rm = TRUE) * 0.92,
    label = paste0("r = ", round(cor_val, 2)),
    size = 4.5, color = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_color_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    name      = "Distance (km)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Sensor distance predicts ground-satellite disagreement",
    subtitle = "Each point = one Delhi ward (n = 290) | LOESS fit with 95% CI",
    x        = "Distance to nearest CPCB station (km)",
    y        = expression(paste("|Delta| PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3))),
    caption  = "November 2022 | Source: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + CPCB CAAQMS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(family = "Arial"),
    legend.position  = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth       = unit(12, "lines"),
    barheight      = unit(0.5, "lines"),
    title.position = "top"
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig6_distance_vs_disagreement.png"), width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Discussion

## Seasonal pattern

The satellite data and the ground data both confirm the well-documented
pollution cycle of Delhi (refer to the seasonal line chart). PM2.5 peaks
sharply from October to January. The causes are crop residue burning in
neighboring states (Punjab, Haryana), temperature inversions, and lower wind
speeds. During the monsoon, PM2.5 decreases sharply. Delhi exceeds the WHO
annual guideline in every month, and the relatively "clean" monsoon months
also have values far above the safe limits.

The ground readings are consistently higher than the satellite estimates. This
is expected. CPCB stations are often near pollution sources, to measure the
worst-case exposure. A satellite value is a spatial mean over a full 1 km
pixel.

## Spatial heterogeneity

The November heatmap and the ward choropleth show that pollution is not
uniform across the 290 wards of Delhi. Peripheral wards have higher PM2.5.
City-level aggregate statistics do not show this difference.

## Monitoring gap

The gap analysis answers the primary policy question. Across the 290 wards,
the wards farthest from their nearest CPCB station usually have the largest
disagreement between satellite estimates and ground readings (refer to the
scatter plot). With 290 data points, the LOESS fit is statistically
meaningful. It shows the non-linear structure of this relation. The priority
map shows the wards where a new station will have the largest effect. These
wards have above-median satellite PM2.5 and poor sensor coverage (>2 km from
the nearest station).

---

# Limitations

- The delta values are negative. Ground stations consistently read higher than
  satellite estimates because of the point-source siting bias. Thus, the
  analysis uses the *relative* disagreement across wards. It does not use the
  absolute values.

- `cpcb_add_coords()` gets the station coordinates directly from the CPCB live
  feed. Nominatim geocoding is the fallback. All 46 Delhi stations have valid
  coordinates.

- The satellite data version V5GL04 covers 1998 to 2022. When the newer V6GL02
  version is available, the same method will work for any year.

- The BharatViz ward dataset (290 wards) from `geo.bharatviz.org` covers all of
  Delhi, with the NDMC and cantonment areas.
